territorial_scope.description: Applies to any provider that develops, deploys or operates a conversational AI or companion system made available to Hawaii residents, which can reach entities outside the State.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: HB 1782 would add a part to Hawaii Revised Statutes Chapter 481B requiring providers of conversational AI and companion systems available to Hawaii residents to disclose AI status to known minors, restrict specified engagement practices, adopt a minor protection plan, and offer parental tools. Effective January 1, 2077.
summary.long: As introduced, HB 1782 would add a part to Hawaii Revised Statutes Chapter 481B on AI companion system safety for minors. It defines key terms and excludes narrow task, customer-service, developer and internal-only systems. Providers that know or have reasonable certainty a user is a minor must disclose AI status at session start and at least every three hours, and must not allow representations that the system is human, capable of a romantic or sexual relationship, has independent emotions, or provides professional mental health services, nor personalized outputs discouraging disengagement. Providers must take reasonable measures against sexually explicit or self-harm content for minors and direct at-risk users to crisis resources. Each provider must adopt and publish a minor protection plan, review it annually, and submit risk assessment summaries to the office of consumer protection before deploying new or substantially modified services. Providers must offer parental tools and apply age assurance. Enforcement is by the attorney general or the executive director of the office of consumer protection; private actions are barred; violations may draw injunctive relief and civil penalties up to $15,000 per violation, per day; good-faith compliance is a defense. Effective January 1, 2077.

notes: Section 5 sets the effective date as "January 1, 2077", which looks like a typographical error and should be checked against the enacted text. Enforcement subsection (b) refers to "subsection (e)", which concerns cumulative duties, so the reference may be unclear. The minor protection plan is called a "minor protection plan" in subsection (a) and (d) but a "protocol" in subsections (b) and (c). The definition of 'sensitive data' uses "personal data", which the text does not define. The new part's Part and section numbers are blank placeholders. The text is the introduced bill, with no version or enactment history, so relations reflect the bill only.
